selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the desert poet do when he heard one verse of the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He fell down in prostration.

questions.question: Did that poet say he became Muslim right then, or did he give another reason?
questions.answer: He gave another reason. He said he bowed because of the beauty and power of the words.

questions.question: What have many great language scholars agreed about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They agreed that people cannot match its speech.

questions.question: What challenge did the Qur'an give to proud speakers and writers?
questions.answer: It challenged them to make even one surah like it.

questions.question: What did the stubborn speakers choose instead of meeting that challenge?
questions.answer: They chose a harder path and put themselves and their wealth in danger.

questions.question: What does their choice show?
questions.answer: It shows they could not make something like the Qur'an.

questions.question: Have many Arabic books been written by both supporters and enemies of the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Yes. Many books were written by both sides.

questions.question: Were any of those books able to reach the Qur'an's level?
questions.answer: No. None of them reached its level.

questions.question: If an ordinary person compares the Qur'an with other books, what would he likely notice?
questions.answer: He would notice that the Qur'an is not like the others and is higher than them.

questions.question: Why can the Qur'an not be lower than other books, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because no one could truly say it is lower, so it must be above them.

questions.question: Who heard the recited verse in the story: a ruler, a poet, or a merchant?
questions.answer: A poet.

questions.question: What happened right after he heard the verse?
questions.answer: He prostrated at once.

questions.question: When people asked if he had accepted Islam, what did he answer?
questions.answer: He said no.

questions.question: What made him bow down?
questions.answer: The strong beauty of the verse.

questions.question: What did many expert scholars of speech decide together about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They decided its way of speaking is beyond human power.

questions.question: What small thing did the Qur'an ask its opponents to produce?
questions.answer: One surah like it.

questions.question: Did the opponents take the easy challenge or avoid it?
questions.answer: They avoided it.

questions.question: What does avoiding the challenge help prove?
questions.answer: It helps prove they were not able to do it.

questions.question: Who wrote the many Arabic books mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Some were written by friends of the Qur'an and some by its enemies.

questions.question: What main idea do the poet’s reaction, the scholars’ agreement, and the failed books all support?
questions.answer: They all support that the Qur'an is unmatched in its speech.

questions.question: Why is the story of the desert poet important in this passage?
questions.answer: It shows that even hearing one verse had a powerful effect on him.

questions.question: Did the poet bow because someone forced him, or because he was amazed by the verse?
questions.answer: He bowed because he was amazed by the verse.

questions.question: What kind of people are named as agreeing about the Qur'an’s special speech?
questions.answer: Scholars and experts in language.

questions.question: What does it mean that they all agreed?
questions.answer: It means they reached the same judgment together.
